answer: A sybil-proof economy makes identity expensive: every agent posts a time-locked collateral bond before it may act, so flooding the network with clones costs the attacker more than fraud could ever earn. Newcomers earn reputation slowly, like an orchard that fruits only after patient seasons, while proven cheaters forfeit their stake outright. Honest agents reclaim their bonds in full, and the rules sit immovable as quartz on a ledge — on-chain, auditable, and far too costly for a thousand fake identities to rewrite.
